headline: Iran claims fourth tanker hit by mine, catches fire in Strait of Hormuz
description: IRGC says supertanker ignored warnings against using an unauthorised shipping route
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claimed that a fourth oil tanker had struck a naval mine and caught fire while attempting to pass through what it described as an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC Navy’s public relations office said on Friday the supertanker, carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil, had ignored repeated radio warnings against using the southern passage through the strategic waterway.

The vessel subsequently struck a mine, triggering a powerful explosion and setting it ablaze, according to the statement.

The IRGC said the tanker had been attempting to exit the strait through an unauthorised southern route.

It claimed the incident was the fourth tanker fire in the Strait of Hormuz since early Friday.

Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that a vessel had been hit by an unidentified projectile about 40 nautical miles south of Iran’s Lavan Island at 1800 GMT.

The projectile struck the vessel’s port side and caused a fire on board, the UKMTO said, adding that all crew members were safe and no environmental impact had been reported.

It was not immediately clear whether the incident reported by the UKMTO was connected to the tanker mentioned by the IRGC.

Iranian authorities have reported several incidents involving commercial vessels in and around the strait in recent weeks, including tankers allegedly damaged by naval mines.

The Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, is a vital international shipping route for oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

headline: After Louvre heist and string of thefts, Europe's smaller museums are on guard
description: High-profile heists expose security gaps at cultural institutions with limited resources
author: Reuters
article_text:
Two men wearing head torches climbed through a forced-open window at the Fondazione Magnani Rocca museum near Parma on the night of March 22 and calmly lifted artworks by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse from the walls.

Within three minutes, they had passed the works, valued at about €9 million ($10 million), to an accomplice and fled.

At the museum’s main gate, a fourth man discharged a fire extinguisher when the alarm sounded, distracting the ​custodian.

“Whatever could go wrong, did,” said Stefano Roffi, director of the private foundation that runs the museum.

The raid was one of a string of museum thefts in France, Italy and Spain since last year’s heist at ‌the Louvre in Paris, raising concerns that criminals are increasingly targeting smaller institutions with fewer resources to protect valuable collections.

“This is where we see the ‘Louvre effect’,” said Marc Balcells, a Barcelona-based researcher specialising in crimes against cultural heritage. “If the Louvre was so easy to rob, just imagine a tiny museum in a rural area or a smaller town.”

Works by Antonello da Messina vanished from a museum in his Sicilian hometown in August, while two Renoirs were stolen from Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera the following month.

In Spain, thieves stole hundreds of historic gold coins from museums in Badajoz and Albacete and made ​off with a Bronze Age treasure in Villena, near Alicante.

A 2024 survey by France’s Culture Ministry found only one in four cultural institutions had an emergency and risk-prevention plan, while nearly half lacked video surveillance.

Who checks when the alarm goes off?

A French parliamentary report in May said museums lacked the resources and preparation to adequately protect artworks and artefacts.

In Italy, the challenge is amplified by the way the country’s ⁠cultural heritage is spread across hundreds of towns and institutions, a legacy of centuries of fragmented rule.

“That is also what makes our system distinctive: works remain in the places where they were created,” said Antonella Pinna, president of the Italian committee of the ​International Council of Museums. “But we need to make life harder for criminals.”

The council worked with Italy’s Culture Ministry and the Carabinieri on museum security guidelines published in 2015, but Pinna said technology alone was not enough.

“If an alarm goes off, someone has to ​make sure it is checked,” she said.

In a narrow street in the Tuscan town of Sansepolcro, the civic museum displays four works by Renaissance master Piero della Francesca, born just steps away in the 15th century.

The Louvre theft “affected us deeply because cultural heritage is central to Sansepolcro’s identity. It is our soul,” culture councillor Francesca Mercati told Reuters.

After the Louvre raid, officers from the Carabinieri’s cultural heritage protection unit recommended more cameras, longer retention of CCTV footage and tighter controls on bags and bulky clothing.

“We immediately implemented those recommendations,” Mercati said.

A vast network to protect

The scale of the challenge ​is daunting.

Italy has more than 4,400 museums and similar institutions, according to the national statistics agency ISTAT. Spain has about 1,500 museums, while France has more than 1,200 institutions carrying the official “Musees de France” designation, alongside hundreds of smaller collections.

Protecting such a broad ​network is particularly difficult for smaller institutions that depend on local funding.

Florence Imbert, a Paris-based security consultant for cultural institutions, said local authorities ran 85% of small French museums with limited financial resources.

“The budget is key to winning the war,” she said.

France’s Culture Ministry announced ‌a 33-point security ⁠plan in July, backed by €30 million over three years for local museums.

Recent figures suggest concern is warranted. The Carabinieri art squad recorded 17 thefts from Italian museums and galleries in 2025, up from 14 a year earlier.

Europol said in an August report that museum thefts were becoming more forceful and increasingly focused on precious metals, gemstones and other high-value artefacts.

A fast buck?

Unlike gold or jewellery, which can be broken up or melted down, a well-known painting is difficult to turn into quick cash.

Celebrated works such as those by Renoir can rarely be sold openly, Pinna said. Instead, stolen art is more likely to be hidden, used as leverage in ransom attempts or offered privately.

Even when works are recovered, museums can face significant costs linked to investigations, recovery efforts and upgraded security.

The recent ​thefts have also reignited debate about insurance.

Most major state-backed museums in ​Western Europe rely on government indemnity schemes rather than ⁠commercial cover, but some institutions have begun reassessing the risks, said Filippo Guerrini-Maraldi, a private wealth and fine art insurance specialist at broker Howden Speciality.

“And for the first time, really, in my 40-year career, I’ve seen art theft now becoming more of a major, major risk. It was always the minor risk,” he said.

Insurers are also turning to technology. Beazley is exploring how AI can ​be used to analyse CCTV footage to identify suspicious behaviour in museums and galleries, helping security staff spot threats sooner, said fine art underwriter Dishni Mahendran.

Security vs access

For museum directors ​and cultural officials, the challenge is ⁠how to tighten security without cutting collections off from local communities or diminishing the visitor experience.

“Ultimately, museums must remain easy to access,” Imbert said. “People should be able to enter without having to pass through 50 security checks.”

Julien Volper, a conservator at Belgium’s Africa Museum, said particularly vulnerable treasures should only be displayed when adequate security measures are in place.

“I’m not saying that’s the ultimate solution, but it seems better than displaying replicas,” he said. “We’re not at Disneyland.”

In August, the Carabinieri recovered the three artworks stolen from the Parma museum from a cardboard box ⁠hidden in an ​apartment. Authorities arrested five Moldovan nationals in connection with the theft.

Investigators said wiretaps indicated the suspects had unsuccessfully tried to find buyers in Eastern Europe ​and Russia.

The works have since returned to the museum in what Roffi called a “homecoming party”.

“The theft triggered an outpouring of solidarity in Italy and abroad,” he said. The museum now has round-the-clock guards funded by a local cheese consortium.

“It was seen not simply as a theft from a museum, but as an attack ​on art as a shared cultural heritage.”

headline: Japanese bodybuilder, 90, flexes ageless ambition on Spanish stage
description: 90-year-old Toshisuke Kanazawa plans another competition at 93, hoping to inspire older generations
author: Reuters
article_text:
Nonagenarian Japanese bodybuilder Toshisuke Kanazawa took to the stage on Spain’s Costa del Maresme on Friday, aiming to prove that ​age is no barrier to peak physical fitness.

The 90-year-old travelled to the coastal ‌town of Santa Susanna to compete against rivals decades his junior in the masters category for athletes aged 50 and older in a competition held by the International Fitness and Bodybuilding Federation.

Backstage, Kanazawa mirrored the ​preparations of younger competitors, warming up with his team and applying spray tan ​before flexing under the stage lights.

“I like to try doing things that ⁠nobody else has done, and more than anything I want to pursue bodybuilding for the ​rest of my life,” Kanazawa said.

Kanazawa credits his longevity and conditioning to strict dietary habits, ​saying that a routine established decades ago has kept him robust.

“This is something I’ve been researching and want to learn more about. But ever since I turned 50, I’ve been building muscle by eating a purely ​Japanese diet: brown rice, natto (a fermented soya bean dish), and miso soup,” he said.

“It’s ​really the classic Japanese way of eating. And thanks to that, I’ve gone 90 years without ever getting ‌sick.”

Though ⁠he did not finish on the podium, Kanazawa remains focused on pushing the sport’s boundaries, outlining plans for one final appearance before stepping away from competition.

“I’m thinking I might give it one more go at 93. After that, I’ll probably have to retire,” he said.

“As you ​get older, you start ​developing wrinkles, quite ⁠a lot of them. In Japan, there’s this idea that once you get those wrinkles, it just doesn’t look very good anymore.”

Ultimately, Kanazawa ​hopes his perseverance inspires older generations to remain active and challenge ​conventional limits.

“Once you ⁠set your mind to something, you need to develop the mental strength and determination to see it through no matter what,” Kanazawa said.

“I want people to work hard just as I ⁠have. I ​believe that if they do, we’ll see more people ​like me even as they get older. That’s what I hope for, and I want to be a good ​role model.”

headline: Suspect in bride’s murder killed in alleged police encounter
description: CCD says Sarfraz hit by gunfire from his own accomplices; another suspect arrested
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The prime suspect in the murder of a bride on her wedding reception day in Gujranwala was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD), according to sources on Saturday.

The sources said that four men riding two motorcycles opened fire on CCD personnel after spotting them on Madu Khalil Road.

One of the suspects was injured in the exchange of fire, while the other three managed to escape.

The injured suspect was identified as Sarfraz, who died while being shifted to the hospital.

According to the CCD, he was hit by gunfire from his own accomplices.

CCD officials said Sarfraz had fled to Karachi after allegedly killing the bride and later attempted to go into hiding in Balochistan.

CCD teams pursued him in Sindh and Balochistan before he returned and encountered personnel near Madu Khalil Road.

In a separate operation, the CCD arrested Sarfraz’s accomplice, Hamza, while a woman named Aroob, who was also nominated in the murder case, had already been taken into custody.

Sarfraz allegedly shot dead bride Saba on October 24 near Samanabad Chungi in Gujranwala over her decision to marry someone else.

headline: US plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants, report says
description: Many immigrants facing removal fled Afghanistan after the 2021 Taliban takeover
author: Reuters
article_text:
The administration of US President Donald Trump plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants to Afghanistan, including people who fled the country following the Taliban takeover in 2021, according to US officials and advocacy groups.

Shawn VanDiver, head of the #AfghanEvac coalition, said many of those facing removal had left Afghanistan after the withdrawal of US forces and the Taliban’s return to power.

Some of those facing deportation are “brothers and sons of men who served alongside US forces, families the Taliban already has every reason to target,” VanDiver said.

The New York Times reported that more than 150 Afghan immigrants were expected to be deported in what could be one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans from the United States.

The newspaper said US authorities had detained dozens of Afghan immigrants in Louisiana and planned to deport them, with the first flight expected as early as Monday.

A US official said the deportations would be carried out through Pakistan, as Washington cannot arrange direct removals to Afghanistan because it has no diplomatic ties with the Taliban government.

The Trump administration has defended its immigration crackdown and deportation drive as measures aimed at improving domestic security.

However, rights advocates have criticised the policies, arguing that they undermine due process and freedom of speech and create an unsafe environment for minority communities. Concerns have also been raised over alleged racial profiling.

The US Department of Homeland Security declined to confirm any planned removal operations, citing operational security.

VanDiver urged Congress to pass legislation granting Afghans in the United States temporary protected status to shield them from deportation.

headline: US approves $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
description: Missiles, yet to be manufactured, are not expected to be delivered until the 2030s
author: Reuters
article_text:
The US State Department said it had approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 ‌missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion, in what would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since the start of the second Trump administration.

Delayed missile deliveries have added to Ukraine’s tensions with the US after President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky ​for Ukraine’s unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries.

Ukraine has long said it urgently needs more missile interceptors to knock down ​the growing waves of missiles Russia’s military fires at the country.

The Patriot missile system is the most effective ⁠weapon to counter fast-moving ballistic missiles.

On Thursday, a Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people on a crowded rail platform in the Ukrainian ​city of Dnipro, while 5 died in daytime strikes on two other provincial cities and a late-evening missile strike killed 1 person in the ​capital Kyiv, officials said.

Zelensky said on Monday that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

But despite Ukraine’s urgency, it will likely not receive the missile interceptors quickly.

Weapons sales typically take years to fulfil, and ​two people briefed on the US decision said the missiles — which are yet to be manufactured — are not expected to be delivered until ​a couple of years into the 2030s.

One of the people said Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence is encouraging the Pentagon to bring forward the delivery date, possibly by ‌giving Kyiv ⁠missiles already in the US arsenal and backfilling with the new Patriot interceptors.

Ukraine will pay for the missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through a program called US JUMPSTART, along with national funds financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in a statement.

The programme uses donations from allies to buy weapons, services and training for Ukraine to support its self-defence following Russia’s invasion, according to ​a Pentagon website.

The JUMPSTART programme was ​used in August to buy ⁠3,350 air-launched cruise missiles worth $825 million made by Zone 5 Technologies and CoAspire.

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale of the Patriot interceptors.

The US has supplied large quantities of weapons to allies while also ​using munitions in its own military operations in Iran, raising concerns about inventories of key air defence ​and precision-guided weapons.

In July, ⁠the US Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6 billion to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

Lockheed has said that deal would allow it to follow through on a promise to triple PAC-3 MSE production capacity by the end of 2030 and increase jobs at its Camden, Arkansas, plant by 50%, to ⁠about 1,850 ​from 1,200.

Lockheed previously announced Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would go to 2,000 units ​annually.

Pentagon negotiators are pressing contractors to move much faster, with tentative production agreements struck earlier this year at the centre of efforts to increase missile output.

headline: Pakistan win toss, bowl first against Sri Lanka in final
description: Hosts eye their maiden ODI tri-nation series title on home soil at Gaddafi Stadium
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan won the toss and elected to field first against Sri Lanka in the final of the tri-nation One-Day International (ODI) series in Lahore on Saturday.

The two teams are facing off at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, with the series trophy at stake.

Pakistan have made one change to their playing XI, bringing in Faheem Ashraf in place of Shadab Khan.

Ahead of the final, the captains of both sides took part in a trophy photoshoot at the Governor’s House in Lahore.

Pakistan won both their matches against England and one of their two encounters against Sri Lanka during the tri-series.

The hosts are aiming to win their first-ever ODI tri-nation series title on home soil.

Pakistan became the first team to qualify for the final after registering two victories against England and one against Sri Lanka.

The hosts will be looking to win their maiden ODI tri-series title on home soil.

The ongoing tournament is the fourth ODI tri-series to be held in Pakistan.

headline: Egypt fears escalation in Iran war would be more destructive
description: Foreign minister urges both sides to learn from previous failed efforts to secure a lasting ceasefire
author: Reuters
article_text:
Egypt’s Foreign ​Minister Badr Abdelatty said on Saturday he ‌was “extremely worried” that a new escalation in the war between the United States and Iran ​would be more destructive and have ​a major impact.

He was speaking at the ⁠IISS Manama Dialogue security summit in ​Bahrain.

“The second round will be more dangerous, more ​destructive, and it will lead to nowhere. We have to draw lessons from the past,” he ​said.

An interim agreement reached in June failed ​to secure a lasting ceasefire in the Iran war ‌or ⁠restore normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has since proposed that Washington lift its blockade of Iranian ports ​in exchange for ​Tehran ⁠reopening the disrupted waterway within seven days.

Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on ​Friday in a renewed effort to ​broker ⁠a deal, but the sides remain divided over whether nuclear negotiations or relief from ⁠the ​blockade and oil sanctions ​should come first.

headline: Qatar mediates US-Iran talks to avert renewed war
description: More than 12 hours of talks held in Tehran to revive direct negotiations between US and Iran
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Qatari mediators held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran on Friday to secure an agreement that would restore direct negotiations between the United States and Iran and avert a renewed outbreak of war, diplomatic sources said, as regional tensions mount ahead of the US midterm elections.

The discussions are due to continue in Doha on Saturday, with mediators seeking reciprocal steps from Washington and Tehran to break the deadlock and bring both sides back to the negotiating table over Iran’s nuclear programme and other issues.

A diplomatic source said Qatar remained in regular contact with the White House throughout Friday’s talks, adding that there had been “positive progress” towards a possible agreement.

The mediators are pressing both sides to accept a series of measures that could be implemented over several days to pave the way for direct negotiations.

A US official said the talks remained stalled over competing demands: the Trump administration wants Iran to make nuclear concessions before negotiations resume, while Tehran insists Washington first lift its naval blockade, release frozen Iranian funds and allow the country to sell oil.

Qatar is also seeking to persuade Iran to allow United Nations inspectors to visit nuclear sites damaged in earlier strikes, as a confidence-building measure that could be met with some sanctions relief from Washington.

Differences within US President Donald Trump’s inner circle are also shaping Washington’s approach, with officials divided over whether to pursue diplomacy or further military action against Iran.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are deeply sceptical that a nuclear agreement can be reached with Iran’s current leadership and believe Trump should focus on further weakening the Iranian regime, including through additional strikes, a US official said.

Vice President JD Vance and Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, meanwhile, favour resuming negotiations, although Trump remains doubtful that Tehran will agree to a deal acceptable to him, the official added.

“There are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking,” Trump told reporters on Friday, adding that Washington had time to consider its options. “It’s a war, but it is not a typical war,” he said.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is overseeing an economic pressure campaign known as “Operation Economic Outcast”, is among Trump’s close advisers urging him to allow the initiative to run its course rather than rush into renewed military action.

One US official suggested Trump could be more inclined to order a major military operation if Republicans suffer heavy losses in the elections, arguing that Tehran’s best opportunity to secure a deal was before the vote.

However, a White House official said the election results would not influence Trump’s decisions on Iran.

The leaders of Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have urged Trump in recent days to give diplomacy more time.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, by contrast, is lobbying for a joint US-Israeli operation against Iran immediately after the elections.

headline: LPG price increased by Rs14.73 per kg for November

According to the OGRA notification, the new price of a domestic LPG cylinder has been fixed at Rs3,470.09, up from Rs3,296.23 in October.

The revised LPG prices will take effect from November 1.

headline: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to cast ballot in US election
description: American-born pontiff casts ballot in Chicago while keeping his candidate choices private
author: Reuters
article_text:
Pope Leo XIV cast a ballot by mail in the US ​midterm elections, the Vatican press office said on Friday, a historic ‌first for the American-born pontiff.

“In keeping with this long-standing practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago,” the Vatican said.

“The Holy Father expresses his belief ​in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic ​processes.”

The Vatican did not say which candidates Leo had voted for.

Leo, ⁠71, was born in Chicago and is the first American-born pope.

The pope ​voted by mail under his birth name, Robert Francis Prevost, according to the Will County ​Clerk’s website.

President Donald Trump’s sagging popularity is hurting his fellow Republicans’ chances of holding onto their majorities in both chambers of Congress in the November 3 election, with the public ​unhappy about the high cost of living and the Iran war.

Trump repeatedly criticised ​Leo early in the new pope’s tenure, calling him “weak” and “terrible” on crime.

The pope said in March that ‌God ⁠rejects the prayers of those who start wars and have “hands full of blood.”

In April, he termed Trump’s threat to destroy the Iranian civilisation as unacceptable and previously declined to join the US president’s so-called “Board of Peace” initiative for Gaza.

Leo ​has also urged a “deep ​reflection” on the ⁠way migrants are treated in the US.

Voters in the solidly Democratic state of Illinois will select a successor for ​retiring US Senator Dick Durbin and choose whether to re-elect ​Governor JB ⁠Pritzker.

Leo was elected to lead the 1.4-billion-member Church by the world’s cardinals in May 2025.

The pope had the lower lobe of his right lung removed in surgery on ⁠October ​13 and was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the ​most common form of lung cancer.

Doctors say he will not need further therapy.

He is set to ​travel to South America next week.

headline: World Bank approves $150m to boost property tax collection in Karachi
description: The initiative aims to raise Karachi’s annual property tax revenue from $8.5m to $85m
author: APP
article_text:
The World Bank Group’s Board of Executive Directors has approved $150 million in financing for a programme aimed at improving urban property tax collection and strengthening municipal service delivery in Sindh, particularly Karachi.

The Sindh Property Revenues Enhancement Programme (Sindh PREP) would support the provincial government in improving urban immovable property tax (UIPT) collection and strengthening the service delivery capacity of selected local councils, a WB news release said on Saturday.

“Cities that can raise their own revenues can plan and invest for the long term,” World Bank Country Director for Pakistan Bolormaa Amgaabazar said.

She said Sindh’s local councils currently depended on provincial transfers for more than 95 per cent of their revenues.

By helping Karachi collect property taxes from residents and businesses and reinvesting most of the revenue in local services, the country director said the programme would enable cities to finance the infrastructure they needed.

Despite being one of the world’s largest cities, Karachi currently collects only around $8.5 million annually in property taxes, while cities of comparable size collect 82 to 350 times more.

The programme aims to increase Karachi’s annual property tax collection to $85 million by raising compliance from 20 to 50 per cent.

It would strengthen tax collection, compliance and administration through a property tax management information system covering billing, payment processing and grievance redress, alongside integrated financial management information systems across local councils.

About 70 per cent of the collected property tax revenue will be reinvested directly in municipal infrastructure and services in participating local councils.

The programme would benefit Karachi’s 25 local councils, covering 3.58 million people.

Its performance-based financing mechanism would link funding to annual assessments conducted by an Independent Verification Agent, with the resulting allocations used to rehabilitate climate-resilient municipal infrastructure and improve services.

The investments would cover drainage, sewerage, schools, fire stations, roads and street lighting.

The programme also includes a $40 million Investment Project Financing component to expand property surveys and property tax administration to 20 local councils in other urban centres of Sindh, indirectly benefiting around 4.5 million people.

“Karachi has significant untapped potential to generate revenues from its property base and use those resources to fund the infrastructure its residents and businesses need,” said Davison Muchadenyika, Senior Urban Development Specialist at the World Bank.

He said the programme would help Sindh strengthen fiscal sustainability, enabling cities to plan, invest and deliver services effectively through their own resources.

The investments would cover drainage, sewerage, schools, fire stations, roads and street lighting.

The programme also includes a $40 million Investment Project Financing component to expand property surveys and property tax administration to 20 local councils in other urban centres of Sindh, indirectly benefiting around 4.5 million people.

“Karachi has significant untapped potential to generate revenues from its property base and use those resources to fund the infrastructure its residents and businesses need,” said Davison Muchadenyika, Senior Urban Development Specialist at the World Bank.
He said the programme would help Sindh strengthen fiscal sustainability, enabling cities to plan, invest and deliver services effectively through their own resources.

headline: Moammar Rana’s wife obtains khula decree, refuses reconciliation
description: Mehnaz Moammar Rana declines to resume her marriage with the Pakistani film actor
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Mehnaz Moammar Rana, wife of Pakistani film actor Moammar Rana, has obtained a khula decree after refusing reconciliation, according to reports.

Mehnaz secured the decree through her lawyer, Barrister Khadija Siddiqui, after making it clear during the proceedings that she did not wish to continue her marriage with the actor.

Her refusal to reconcile was followed by the issuance of the khula decree, formally ending the marriage.

The development has drawn attention because of Moammar Rana’s prominence in Pakistan’s film industry.

However, the available reports did not disclose the reasons behind the separation or provide further details about the couple’s personal circumstances.

headline: Shehbaz asks what PTI did for KP during 13 years in power
description: PM questions lack of universities, hospitals and Safe City projects for people in the province
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has reaffirmed his commitment to continue efforts for the development and prosperity of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the welfare of its people.

He was addressing the PML-N Parliamentary Party and office-bearers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Saturday.

The prime minister said governor’s rule and emergency were imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in view of unavoidable circumstances.

He said the decision had become necessary to safeguard the people, the country, the economy and society.

He said failure to take a timely decision could have caused further losses to the province.

The prime minister said the party which remained in power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for the last 13 years only made tall claims, questioning how many universities and hospitals were established there during this period.

He said instead of serving the people, the focus remained on political slogans and deepening divisions.

He said the province has so far received Rs800 billion under the NFC Award.

He questioned how many Safe City projects had been established with these funds and what steps were taken to strengthen the Counter Terrorism Department there.

Shehbaz Sharif said the available resources in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa should have been spent on equipping the police with modern weapons and providing them with training.

He said the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have rendered immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, saying these can never be forgotten.

The prime minister said that during the tenure of prime minister Nawaz Sharif, terrorism was eliminated from the country.

He regretted that the terrorists were brought back from Afghanistan and resettled in Pakistan in 2019 and 2020.

He said the resurgence of terrorism caused huge losses to the country.

Shehbaz said the country’s military and political leadership have worked together to stabilise the national economy.

He said global developments and the Gulf war have led to an extraordinary increase in energy prices.

Despite the challenges, the government launched a fuel subsidy scheme to provide relief to the people.

He said 13 million people have benefited from the fuel subsidy scheme.

Shehbaz said providing relief to the poor is a key priority of the government.

He said all possible measures are being taken to protect the national economy from instability.

headline: Tarar proposes national council to tackle cybersecurity threats
description: Proposed body would bring federal and provincial govts together to promote digital literacy
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday proposed setting up a National Cybersecurity and Social Media Awareness Council to protect citizens from digital threats and promote digital literacy across the country.

Speaking at the inaugural ceremony of Cyber Security Awareness Week 2026, organised by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) in Islamabad, Tarar said provincial governments, federal ministries and divisions, and other organisations could be made members of the proposed council, Radio Pakistan said in a report.

He pledged his full support for the initiative, saying it would help ensure that awareness campaigns were conducted at every level throughout the year.

The minister stressed the need for a coordinated approach to cybersecurity, given its wide-ranging challenges and the need to reach citizens across the country.

He also called for digital literacy to be incorporated into school, college and university curricula to educate students about emerging technological threats and ways to deal with them.

Tarar said a research-based system should be introduced to ensure that educational content was regularly updated in line with rapidly evolving technology.

He added that digital literacy should be made compulsory for all citizens.

The minister also urged every organisation in the country to establish a digital literacy cell and called for officers and government officials to receive training in the field.

headline: UK PM open to formal apology for Britain's role in slavery
description: PM Andy Burnham rules out financial reparations ahead of Commonwealth summit
author: Reuters
article_text:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he is open to calls for a formal apology for Britain’s historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week’s Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was “offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”, in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

“Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them,” he added.

But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: “I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part.”

From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was “only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past”.

Caribbean leaders are expected to press demands for reparations, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.

Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the Guardian that he wanted to “launch a new drive on debt”, including by helping more vulnerable countries “repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates”.

Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham’s ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a Facebook post: “The Caribbean’s longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged.”

headline: Bangladesh records deadliest dengue month of 2026 as deaths reach 418
description: Experts warn outbreak is likely to persist until December, putting further pressure on hospitals
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh recorded its highest monthly dengue death toll of the year in October, with experts warning the outbreak is unlikely to ease significantly before December.

The outbreak has killed 418 people and led to ​more than 133,000 hospital admissions this year as of October 30, according to health ministry ‌data.

October alone accounted for 173 deaths, surpassing September’s 148 and making it the deadliest month of 2026 so far.

The surge comes as Bangladesh is also battling the world’s worst measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,200 people, placing additional strain on an already stretched ​healthcare system.

Hospitals under pressure

Doctors said many dengue patients were only seeking hospital admission after developing severe ​complications.

At the state-run Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital in Dhaka, 279 dengue patients ⁠were being treated after 67 new admissions in a single day, hospital director Mirza Golam Sarwar said.

“We ​are getting many patients in shock. Their blood pressure is sometimes too low to measure, and their oxygen levels ​are dropping,” he said.

Medicine specialist ABM Abdullah said repeat infections and delays in diagnosis and treatment were driving severe cases and deaths.

“People who have had dengue before may face a greater risk of severe illness if they become infected again,” he said, urging ​people to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek care as soon as symptoms appear.

Dhaka resident Faisal Ferdous, 33, ​was diagnosed with dengue in 2017, 2024 and again earlier this month.

“This time, both my wife and I needed hospital treatment,” ‌said Ferdous, ⁠who is now at home recovering.

Ferdous said the couple fell ill shortly after spending several days at a hospital where their five-year-old son was being treated for an unrelated illness.

“Every bout has been difficult, and after getting it repeatedly, you become increasingly concerned about the risk of severe illness,” he said.

Health experts warn that the circulation ​of all four dengue virus ​serotypes is increasing the ⁠risk of severe disease.

People infected with one strain can later contract another, raising the likelihood of complications. Bangladesh has yet to introduce a dengue vaccine, although authorities ​are considering one as a longer-term measure.

Climate change extends dengue season

Entomologist Kabirul Bashar ​of Jahangirnagar University ⁠said deaths were unlikely to continue rising at October’s pace, but transmission would probably persist through November.

“We may see some relief, but dengue is unlikely to disappear in November. Any decline is likely to be modest, with significant improvement ⁠unlikely before ​December,” he said.

Bashar said mosquitoes would continue emerging from breeding sites ​created by earlier rainfall, sustaining transmission even as conditions become drier.

Changing rainfall and humidity patterns, partly linked to climate change, were extending ​mosquito breeding seasons and keeping Aedes mosquitoes active for longer, he said.

headline: Any new US attack would spread war wider: Iran's army
description: Warning comes as Qatari mediators hold talks in Tehran and Vance’s letter to security chief awaits response
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran’s army warned on Saturday that any new US attack would only spread the war wider, following threats by America and Israel of further military action as they hold crucial elections.

The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts underway to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US Vice President JD Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

“If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said in a post on X, without elaborating.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also warned on Saturday that “Iran’s Powerful Armed Forces will deal with those who dare harm our people”.

On Friday, a Qatari delegation arrived in the Iranian capital for talks with senior Iranian officials.

Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran’s security chief at the direction of President Donald Trump in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.

Iran has confirmed receiving the letter but has not announced any response.

The US holds midterm elections on Tuesday that could determine the direction of the war, which has proven unpopular with American voters following a spike in energy prices due to the conflict.

Last Tuesday, Israel also held legislative elections, with voters given a chance to offer a verdict on right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Under Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran’s government, Israel and Iran have engaged in direct military confrontations after decades of shadow war.

The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that killed the country’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as well as senior military commanders.

Iran, in response, targeted US assets across the Middle East as well as Israel.

Most recently, hostilities have focused on the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial Gulf shipping route for energy exports that Iran has blockaded since the start of the war.

The US has, in retaliation, been blockading Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the nation’s economy.

headline: Qatar announces free 30-day tourist visa on arrival for Pakistanis
description: Travellers must meet four conditions, including a valid passport, confirmed return ticket, Discover Qatar hotel booking and approved health insurance
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Qatar has announced a free tourist visa on arrival for Pakistani citizens, allowing them to stay in the country for up to 30 days without obtaining a visa in advance.

According to information available on the Qatari Ministry of Interior’s official website, the facility is subject to specific requirements that travellers must fulfil before their departure.

Under the arrangement, Pakistani nationals can receive a free visa on arrival for a maximum of 30 days. However, the permitted duration may also depend on the length of their hotel reservation.

To qualify for the facility, travellers must meet four conditions.

First, their passports must have a validity of at least three months at the time of arrival in Qatar. They must also hold a confirmed return ticket.

In addition, visitors are required to book their hotel accommodation exclusively through Qatar’s official tourism platform, Discover Qatar. Reservations made through other websites or online booking platforms will not be accepted under this arrangement.

The fourth requirement is valid health insurance obtained from an insurance company approved by Qatar’s Ministry of Public Health.

The Ministry of Interior has stated that all four conditions must be met to qualify for the free visa on arrival.

Travellers who fail to provide the required documents or meet the eligibility criteria may not be granted the facility.

The arrangement is separate from Qatar’s other visa-free entry arrangements and tourist visa programmes.

Pakistani travellers planning to visit Qatar have been advised to check the requirements and ensure that all necessary documents are in order before travelling.

Further information and hotel booking details are available through Qatar’s official tourism website, Discover Qatar.

headline: Saudi says intercepted 'hostile drone' in Riyadh region
description: Coalition spokesman says debris fell without causing injuries
author: AFP
article_text:
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis.

“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region,” Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that “debris from the interception fell without causing injuries”.

Malki did not say who launched the drone.

In recent weeks, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events — threatening the kingdom’s economic diversification plans.

On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam’s second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.

More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.

In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.

The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

headline: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister
description: Damascus says talks are underway on joining the alliance of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Syria’s top diplomat on Saturday said Damascus was considering whether to join the Makkah defence alliance that binds Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on August 7, 2026, by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, establishes a collective defence framework where an armed attack against any single member is treated as an attack against all three.

“Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria’s entry into the Makkah alliance,” Al Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain.

Saudi Arabia, under heavy fire from Yemen’s Houthis, is a key backer of Syria’s government that came to power after the fall of former strongman Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

Pakistan has two defence agreements with Saudi Arabia aimed at collective deterrence: the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two countries, and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which also includes Turkiye.

Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said earlier this month.

However, the Inter-Services Public Relations director general also clarified that all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance were “absolutely clear… that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”.

On Friday, Lt-Gen Chaudhry said the wording of the pact did not bar new members, when asked whether Iran could join the agreement.

“Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.

Earlier this month, French President Emmanuel Macron made a surprise visit to Riyadh and said France had sent troops to help shield a key Saudi oil terminal from Houthi attacks.

Also in October, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter planes to help Saudi Arabia against the attacks.

description: Confirms Vance letter was received and ‘carefully reviewed’ as mediators consult on Iran’s conditions
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran’s top diplomat on Saturday said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States despite growing concerns over a return to war.

“Currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials, and any speculation to the contrary is merely media assumption,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.

“Under current circumstances, Iran sees no necessity for a meeting with the Americans; Iran’s conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators,” he said.

Araghchi confirmed that Iran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, following days of diplomatic efforts to head off a return to violence.

“The message from American Vice President JD Vance has been carefully reviewed and discussed in high-level meetings,” he said.

“If Washington’s objective in sending the message is to sow discord, this would be yet another misstep, adding to America’s previous errors.”

But Araghchi added: “The American side’s effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step.”

headline: Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
description: Written statement says Iran’s armed forces will decide when any new war ends, as diplomacy to avert renewed fighting continues
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic Republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes.

“If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.

Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.

According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response”.

It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”.

The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.

The supreme leader’s statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were underway to avert a resumption of fighting.

A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance.

According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

headline: Fakhar blitz powers Pakistan to clinch tri-nation ODI title
description: Fakhar and Saad Baig put on 149-run partnership after Pakistan lose two early wickets in tri-series final
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan were in a strong position in their chase of 326 against Sri Lanka in the tri-nation ODI series final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, powered by a brilliant century from Fakhar Zaman.

Pakistan suffered an early setback, losing their first two wickets for just 14 runs inside the fourth over. However, Fakhar and Saad Baig steadied the innings with an impressive 149-run partnership.

Maaz Sadaqat was dismissed for five runs, while Babar Azam returned to the pavilion without scoring. Both fell to Sri Lankan fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka.

Fakhar and Saad then counterattacked with a combination of aggressive and controlled batting to bring Pakistan back into the contest.

Saad scored 74 before being caught and bowled by Maheesh Theekshana in the 27th over.

Fakhar continued his outstanding innings, scoring 127 off 99 balls, including 11 fours and six sixes. He completed his 12th ODI century before being dismissed in the 34th over.

Pakistan suffered another setback shortly afterwards when Salman Ali Agha was also dismissed, giving Sri Lanka an opportunity to fight back.

Madushanka has taken three wickets so far, while Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage have claimed one wicket each.

Earlier, Sri Lanka posted 325-8 in their allotted 50 overs after Pakistan won the toss and elected to field.

Kamindu Mendis led the Sri Lankan batting with a superb 131 off 114 balls, hitting 12 fours and two sixes. Pavan Rathnayake contributed 77 runs, while Oshada Fernando scored 38.

For Pakistan, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf claimed two wickets each. Naseem conceded 80 runs in his 10 overs, while Haris gave away 60.

Pakistan brought in Faheem Ashraf in place of Shadab Khan for the final. Shaheen Shah Afridi is leading the national side, while Kusal Mendis is captaining Sri Lanka.

Pakistan had defeated England in both their matches and beaten Sri Lanka once during the tournament. The hosts are aiming to win their first ODI tri-nation series title on home soil.

headline: UK police arrest Palestine Action supporters ahead of Supreme Court hearing
description: Police say 48 arrested for supporting proscribed group; Supreme Court to hear challenge to ban from Wednesday
author: AFP
article_text:
London police arrested Saturday dozens of Palestine Action supporters, who protested there and in Edinburgh days before the Supreme Court hears an appeal over the government’s contentious ban of the group.

London’s Metropolitan Police began detaining people shortly after hundreds began a lunchtime “mass action” outside the US Embassy in the British capital, an AFP reporter witnessed.

The force said in a mid-afternoon update that 48 people had been arrested and that officers were “continuing to make arrests”.

“The majority of arrests have been for expressing support for a proscribed organisation,” it added on X.

Officers have arrested nearly 4,000 people for allegedly showing support for Palestine Action, according to police and campaigners, after the British government outlawed it under anti-terror laws in July 2025.

Many of those arrested, including senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, have displayed signs at rallies reading: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.”

In July, hearings related to more than 2,000 of those cases were postponed until later this year.

The ban puts the group on a blacklist that also includes Palestinian militants Hamas and the Lebanese Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah.

It made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a criminal offence punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

The group’s co-founder Huda Ammori has legally challenged the ban, arguing it was “disproportionate” and impacted human rights.

The Supreme Court is set to hold a two-day hearing on the high-profile case from Wednesday, after the Court of Appeal in June ruled in the government’s favour.

‘Losing faith’

Saturday’s London protesters held banners bearing slogans like “How is trying to stop a genocide a crime?” and “We are protesters, not terrorists”.

Attendee Angie Zelter, 75, told AFP she had already been charged at least eight times at previous rallies but wanted to protest again ahead of the Supreme Court hearing.

“I am hoping they will come to their senses and agree PA (Palestine Action) should not have been proscribed,” she said.

Marji Mansfield, 70, a retired financial adviser, said she had previously been arrested about 10 times.

“I am losing faith in [the] judicial system,” she told AFP.

“But if they lift the ban, it would be a way out for the government,” Mansfield added, while noting there was currently “no sign” of the ban’s reversal.

A bestselling Irish author, Sally Rooney, has become embroiled in the controversy, with her publisher Faber revealing this month it can no longer sell her books in the UK because she supports the group.

Set up in 2020, Palestine Action’s stated goal on its website — blocked to UK internet users — is to end “global participation in Israel’s genocidal and apartheid regime”.

It gained visibility after Israel began bombarding Gaza following the October 7, 2023, attack by fighters from the Palestinian group Hamas in southern Israel.

article_html:
London police arrested Saturday dozens of Palestine Action supporters, who protested there and in Edinburgh days before the Supreme Court hears an appeal over the government’s contentious ban of the group.

London’s Metropolitan Police began detaining people shortly after hundreds began a lunchtime “mass action” outside the US Embassy in the British capital, an AFP reporter witnessed.

The force said in a mid-afternoon update that 48 people had been arrested and that officers were “continuing to make arrests”.

“The majority of arrests have been for expressing support for a proscribed organisation,” it added on X.

Officers have arrested nearly 4,000 people for allegedly showing support for Palestine Action, according to police and campaigners, after the British government outlawed it under anti-terror laws in July 2025.

Many of those arrested, including senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, have displayed signs at rallies reading: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.”

In July, hearings related to more than 2,000 of those cases were postponed until later this year.

The ban puts the group on a blacklist that also includes Palestinian militants Hamas and the Lebanese Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah.

It made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a criminal offence punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

The group’s co-founder Huda Ammori has legally challenged the ban, arguing it was “disproportionate” and impacted human rights.

The Supreme Court is set to hold a two-day hearing on the high-profile case from Wednesday, after the Court of Appeal in June ruled in the government’s favour.

‘Losing faith’

Saturday’s London protesters held banners bearing slogans like “How is trying to stop a genocide a crime?” and “We are protesters, not terrorists”.

Attendee Angie Zelter, 75, told AFP she had already been charged at least eight times at previous rallies but wanted to protest again ahead of the Supreme Court hearing.

“I am hoping they will come to their senses and agree PA (Palestine Action) should not have been proscribed,” she said.

Marji Mansfield, 70, a retired financial adviser, said she had previously been arrested about 10 times.

“I am losing faith in [the] judicial system,” she told AFP.

“But if they lift the ban, it would be a way out for the government,” Mansfield added, while noting there was currently “no sign” of the ban’s reversal.

A bestselling Irish author, Sally Rooney, has become embroiled in the controversy, with her publisher Faber revealing this month it can no longer sell her books in the UK because she supports the group.

Set up in 2020, Palestine Action’s stated goal on its website — blocked to UK internet users — is to end “global participation in Israel’s genocidal and apartheid regime”.

It gained visibility after Israel began bombarding Gaza following the October 7, 2023, attack by fighters from the Palestinian group Hamas in southern Israel.

The group has mainly targeted weapons factories in Britain, especially those belonging to the Israel-based defence group Elbit.
